scene.label: Act 4, Scene 2
scene.title: SCENE II. A room in the prison.

lines.text: Come hither, sirrah. Can you cut off a man's head?
lines.plainText: Come hither sirrah Can you cut off a man's head

lines.text: If the man be a bachelor, sir, I can; but if he be a married man, he's his wife's head, and I can never cut off a woman's head.
lines.plainText: If the man be a bachelor sir I can but if he be a married man he's his wife's head and I can never cut off a woman's head

lines.text: Come, sir, leave me your snatches, and yield me a direct answer. Tomorrow morning are to die Claudio and Barnardine. Here is in our prison a common executioner, who in his office lacks a helper; if you will take it on you to assist him, it shall redeem you from your gyves; if not, you shall have your full time of imprisonment, and your deliverance with an unpitied whipping; for you have been a notorious bawd.
lines.plainText: Come sir leave me your snatches and yield me a direct answer Tomorrow morning are to die Claudio and Barnardine Here is in our prison a common executioner who in his office lacks a helper if you will take it on you to assist him it shall redeem you from your gyves if not you shall have your full time of imprisonment and your deliverance with an unpitied whipping for you have been a notorious bawd

lines.text: Sir, I have been an unlawful bawd time out of mind, but yet I will be content to be a lawful hangman. I would be glad to receive some instruction from my fellow-partner.
lines.plainText: Sir I have been an unlawful bawd time out of mind but yet I will be content to be a lawful hangman I would be glad to receive some instruction from my fellowpartner

lines.text: What ho, Abhorson! Where's Abhorson, there?
lines.plainText: What ho Abhorson Where's Abhorson there

lines.text: Do you call, sir?
lines.plainText: Do you call sir

lines.text: Sirrah, here's a fellow will help you tomorrow in your execution. If you think it meet, compound with him by the year, and let him abide here with you; if not, use him for the present, and dismiss him. He cannot plead his estimation with you; he hath been a bawd.
lines.plainText: Sirrah here's a fellow will help you tomorrow in your execution If you think it meet compound with him by the year and let him abide here with you if not use him for the present and dismiss him He cannot plead his estimation with you he hath been a bawd

lines.text: A bawd, sir? Fie upon him, he will discredit our mystery.
lines.plainText: A bawd sir Fie upon him he will discredit our mystery

lines.text: Go to, sir; you weigh equally. A feather will turn the scale.
lines.plainText: Go to sir you weigh equally A feather will turn the scale

lines.text: Pray, sir, by your good favour—for surely, sir, a good favour you have, but that you have a hanging look—do you call, sir, your occupation a mystery?
lines.plainText: Pray sir by your good favourfor surely sir a good favour you have but that you have a hanging lookdo you call sir your occupation a mystery

lines.text: Ay, sir, a mystery.
lines.plainText: Ay sir a mystery

lines.text: Painting, sir, I have heard say, is a mystery; and your whores, sir, being members of my occupation, using painting, do prove my occupation a mystery. But what mystery there should be in hanging, if I should be hanged, I cannot imagine.
lines.plainText: Painting sir I have heard say is a mystery and your whores sir being members of my occupation using painting do prove my occupation a mystery But what mystery there should be in hanging if I should be hanged I cannot imagine

lines.text: Sir, it is a mystery.
lines.plainText: Sir it is a mystery

lines.text: Proof.
lines.plainText: Proof

lines.text: Every true man's apparel fits your thief. If it be too little for your thief, your true man thinks it big enough; if it be too big for your thief, your thief thinks it little enough. So every true man's apparel fits your thief.
lines.plainText: Every true man's apparel fits your thief If it be too little for your thief your true man thinks it big enough if it be too big for your thief your thief thinks it little enough So every true man's apparel fits your thief

lines.text: Are you agreed?
lines.plainText: Are you agreed

lines.text: Sir, I will serve him; for I do find your hangman is a more penitent trade than your bawd. He doth oftener ask forgiveness.
lines.plainText: Sir I will serve him for I do find your hangman is a more penitent trade than your bawd He doth oftener ask forgiveness

lines.text: You, sirrah, provide your block and your axe tomorrow four o'clock.
lines.plainText: You sirrah provide your block and your axe tomorrow four o'clock

lines.text: Come on, bawd. I will instruct thee in my trade. Follow.
lines.plainText: Come on bawd I will instruct thee in my trade Follow

lines.text: I do desire to learn, sir; and I hope, if you have occasion to use me for your own turn, you shall find me yare. For truly, sir, for your kindness I owe you a good turn.
lines.plainText: I do desire to learn sir and I hope if you have occasion to use me for your own turn you shall find me yare For truly sir for your kindness I owe you a good turn

lines.text: Call hither Barnardine and Claudio.
lines.plainText: Call hither Barnardine and Claudio

lines.text: As fast locked up in sleep as guiltless labour
lines.plainText: As fast locked up in sleep as guiltless labour

lines.text: When it lies starkly in the traveller's bones.
lines.plainText: When it lies starkly in the traveller's bones

lines.text: He will not wake.
lines.plainText: He will not wake

lines.text: Who can do good on him?
lines.plainText: Who can do good on him

lines.text: Well, go, prepare yourself. [Knocking within.] But hark, what noise?
lines.plainText: Well go prepare yourself Knocking within But hark what noise

lines.text: Heaven give your spirits comfort!
lines.plainText: Heaven give your spirits comfort

lines.text: The best and wholesom'st spirits of the night
lines.plainText: The best and wholesom'st spirits of the night

lines.text: Envelop you, good Provost! Who called here of late?
lines.plainText: Envelop you good Provost Who called here of late

lines.text: None, since the curfew rung.
lines.plainText: None since the curfew rung

lines.text: Not Isabel?
lines.plainText: Not Isabel

lines.text: No.
lines.plainText: No

lines.text: They will then, ere't be long.
lines.plainText: They will then ere't be long

lines.text: What comfort is for Claudio?
lines.plainText: What comfort is for Claudio

lines.text: There's some in hope.
lines.plainText: There's some in hope

lines.text: It is a bitter deputy.
lines.plainText: It is a bitter deputy

lines.text: Not so, not so. His life is paralleled
lines.plainText: Not so not so His life is paralleled

lines.text: Even with the stroke and line of his great justice.
lines.plainText: Even with the stroke and line of his great justice

lines.text: He doth with holy abstinence subdue
lines.plainText: He doth with holy abstinence subdue

lines.text: That in himself which he spurs on his power
lines.plainText: That in himself which he spurs on his power

lines.text: To qualify in others. Were he mealed with that
lines.plainText: To qualify in others Were he mealed with that

lines.text: Which he corrects, then were he tyrannous;
lines.plainText: Which he corrects then were he tyrannous

lines.text: But this being so, he's just.
lines.plainText: But this being so he's just

content.text: [Knocking within. Provost goes to the door.]

lines.text: There he must stay until the officer
lines.plainText: There he must stay until the officer

lines.text: Arise to let him in. He is called up.
lines.plainText: Arise to let him in He is called up

lines.text: Have you no countermand for Claudio yet,
lines.plainText: Have you no countermand for Claudio yet

lines.text: But he must die tomorrow?
lines.plainText: But he must die tomorrow

lines.text: None, sir, none.
lines.plainText: None sir none

lines.text: As near the dawning, Provost, as it is,
lines.plainText: As near the dawning Provost as it is

lines.text: You shall hear more ere morning.
lines.plainText: You shall hear more ere morning

lines.text: Happily
lines.plainText: Happily

lines.text: You something know, yet I believe there comes
lines.plainText: You something know yet I believe there comes

lines.text: No countermand. No such example have we.
lines.plainText: No countermand No such example have we

lines.text: Besides, upon the very siege of justice
lines.plainText: Besides upon the very siege of justice

lines.text: Lord Angelo hath to the public ear
lines.plainText: Lord Angelo hath to the public ear

lines.text: Professed the contrary.
lines.plainText: Professed the contrary

lines.text: And here comes Claudio's pardon.
lines.plainText: And here comes Claudio's pardon

lines.text: My lord hath sent you this note, and by me this further charge: that you swerve not from the smallest article of it, neither in time, matter, or other circumstance. Good morrow; for, as I take it, it is almost day.
lines.plainText: My lord hath sent you this note and by me this further charge that you swerve not from the smallest article of it neither in time matter or other circumstance Good morrow for as I take it it is almost day

lines.text: I shall obey him.
lines.plainText: I shall obey him

lines.text: [Aside.] This is his pardon, purchased by such sin
lines.plainText: Aside This is his pardon purchased by such sin

lines.text: For which the pardoner himself is in.
lines.plainText: For which the pardoner himself is in

lines.text: Hence hath offence his quick celerity,
lines.plainText: Hence hath offence his quick celerity

lines.text: When it is borne in high authority.
lines.plainText: When it is borne in high authority

lines.text: When vice makes mercy, mercy's so extended
lines.plainText: When vice makes mercy mercy's so extended

lines.text: That for the fault's love is th' offender friended.
lines.plainText: That for the fault's love is th' offender friended

lines.text: Now, sir, what news?
lines.plainText: Now sir what news

lines.text: I told you: Lord Angelo, belike thinking me remiss in mine office, awakens me with this unwonted putting-on; methinks strangely, for he hath not used it before.
lines.plainText: I told you Lord Angelo belike thinking me remiss in mine office awakens me with this unwonted puttingon methinks strangely for he hath not used it before

lines.text: Pray you, let's hear.
lines.plainText: Pray you let's hear

lines.text: [Reads.] Whatsoever you may hear to the contrary, let Claudio be executed by four of the clock, and in the afternoon, Barnardine. For my better satisfaction, let me have Claudio's head sent me by five. Let this be duly performed, with a thought that more depends on it than we must yet deliver. Thus fail not to do your office, as you will answer it at your peril.

lines.text: What say you to this, sir?
lines.plainText: What say you to this sir

lines.text: What is that Barnardine who is to be executed in th' afternoon?
lines.plainText: What is that Barnardine who is to be executed in th' afternoon

lines.text: A Bohemian born, but here nursed up and bred; one that is a prisoner nine years old.
lines.plainText: A Bohemian born but here nursed up and bred one that is a prisoner nine years old

lines.text: How came it that the absent Duke had not either delivered him to his liberty, or executed him? I have heard it was ever his manner to do so.
lines.plainText: How came it that the absent Duke had not either delivered him to his liberty or executed him I have heard it was ever his manner to do so

lines.text: His friends still wrought reprieves for him; and indeed, his fact till now in the government of Lord Angelo, came not to an undoubtful proof.
lines.plainText: His friends still wrought reprieves for him and indeed his fact till now in the government of Lord Angelo came not to an undoubtful proof

lines.text: It is now apparent?
lines.plainText: It is now apparent

lines.text: Most manifest, and not denied by himself.
lines.plainText: Most manifest and not denied by himself

lines.text: Hath he borne himself penitently in prison? How seems he to be touched?
lines.plainText: Hath he borne himself penitently in prison How seems he to be touched

lines.text: A man that apprehends death no more dreadfully but as a drunken sleep; careless, reckless, and fearless of what's past, present, or to come; insensible of mortality and desperately mortal.
lines.plainText: A man that apprehends death no more dreadfully but as a drunken sleep careless reckless and fearless of what's past present or to come insensible of mortality and desperately mortal

lines.text: He wants advice.
lines.plainText: He wants advice

lines.text: He will hear none. He hath evermore had the liberty of the prison; give him leave to escape hence, he would not. Drunk many times a day, if not many days entirely drunk. We have very oft awaked him, as if to carry him to execution, and showed him a seeming warrant for it. It hath not moved him at all.
lines.plainText: He will hear none He hath evermore had the liberty of the prison give him leave to escape hence he would not Drunk many times a day if not many days entirely drunk We have very oft awaked him as if to carry him to execution and showed him a seeming warrant for it It hath not moved him at all

lines.text: More of him anon. There is written in your brow, Provost, honesty and constancy; if I read it not truly, my ancient skill beguiles me. But in the boldness of my cunning I will lay myself in hazard. Claudio, whom here you have warrant to execute, is no greater forfeit to the law than Angelo who hath sentenced him. To make you understand this in a manifested effect, I crave but four days' respite, for the which you are to do me both a present and a dangerous courtesy.

lines.text: Pray, sir, in what?
lines.plainText: Pray sir in what

lines.text: In the delaying death.
lines.plainText: In the delaying death

lines.text: Alack, how may I do it? Having the hour limited, and an express command, under penalty, to deliver his head in the view of Angelo? I may make my case as Claudio's, to cross this in the smallest.
lines.plainText: Alack how may I do it Having the hour limited and an express command under penalty to deliver his head in the view of Angelo I may make my case as Claudio's to cross this in the smallest

lines.text: By the vow of mine order, I warrant you, if my instructions may be your guide. Let this Barnardine be this morning executed, and his head borne to Angelo.
lines.plainText: By the vow of mine order I warrant you if my instructions may be your guide Let this Barnardine be this morning executed and his head borne to Angelo

lines.text: Angelo hath seen them both, and will discover the favour.
lines.plainText: Angelo hath seen them both and will discover the favour

lines.text: O, death's a great disguiser, and you may add to it. Shave the head and tie the beard, and say it was the desire of the penitent to be so bared before his death. You know the course is common. If anything fall to you upon this, more than thanks and good fortune, by the saint whom I profess, I will plead against it with my life.

lines.text: Pardon me, good father; it is against my oath.
lines.plainText: Pardon me good father it is against my oath

lines.text: Were you sworn to the Duke, or to the Deputy?
lines.plainText: Were you sworn to the Duke or to the Deputy

lines.text: To him and to his substitutes.
lines.plainText: To him and to his substitutes

lines.text: You will think you have made no offence if the Duke avouch the justice of your dealing?
lines.plainText: You will think you have made no offence if the Duke avouch the justice of your dealing

lines.text: But what likelihood is in that?
lines.plainText: But what likelihood is in that

lines.text: Not a resemblance, but a certainty. Yet since I see you fearful, that neither my coat, integrity, nor persuasion, can with ease attempt you, I will go further than I meant, to pluck all fears out of you. Look you, sir, here is the hand and seal of the Duke. You know the character, I doubt not, and the signet is not strange to you.
lines.plainText: Not a resemblance but a certainty Yet since I see you fearful that neither my coat integrity nor persuasion can with ease attempt you I will go further than I meant to pluck all fears out of you Look you sir here is the hand and seal of the Duke You know the character I doubt not and the signet is not strange to you

lines.text: I know them both.
lines.plainText: I know them both

lines.text: The contents of this is the return of the Duke; you shall anon over-read it at your pleasure, where you shall find within these two days he will be here. This is a thing that Angelo knows not; for he this very day receives letters of strange tenour, perchance of the Duke's death, perchance entering into some monastery; but, by chance, nothing of what is writ. Look, th' unfolding star calls up the shepherd. Put not yourself into amazement how these things should be. All difficulties are but easy when they are known. Call your executioner, and off with Barnardine's head. I will give him a present shrift, and advise him for a better place. Yet you are amazed; but this shall absolutely resolve you. Come away; it is almost clear dawn.
